titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 7/2023 (ކުންފުނީގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Company Act (No. 7/2023). It changes a handful of numbers in Articles 100, 113 and 126, mostly shortening time periods. Article 100 appears to set how many days' notice must be given before a meeting, and the bill changes those day counts. Articles 113 and 126 are also amended, and Article 126 gets a shorter deadline. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain, including what each deadline applies to.
whyItMatters: Companies and the people who run or own them would work to different deadlines under the Act, with several periods getting shorter. The exact obligations could not be read reliably.
keyProvisions: Article 100(a)(1): a period is cut from 21 days to 3 days. It appears to be the notice that must be given before a meeting; the type of meeting could not be read.
Article 100(a)(2): a period is changed from 3 days to 10 days, so this one gets longer.
Article 100(c)(1) and (2): a period in each is cut from 14 days to 7 days.
Article 113: one lettered paragraph is replaced. The printed old and new texts look near-identical, so the change could not be identified.
Article 126(a) and (b): a period in each is cut from 30 days to 10 days. The text refers to Articles 113, 114 and 125; what the deadline applies to could not be read.
The last clause (5) appears to say the amendment takes effect on the date it is ratified.
whoIsAffected: Companies registered under the Company Act and the people who run, own or deal with them.
statedReasons: A short explanatory note is printed on page 2. It says the bill amends the Company Act, but the reasons could not be read reliably.
